checks.title: A schema coordinate is one of the five productions, and nothing else
checks.basis: "SchemaCoordinate :: TypeCoordinate | MemberCoordinate | ArgumentCoordinate | DirectiveCoordinate | DirectiveArgumentCoordinate", with "TypeCoordinate :: Name", "MemberCoordinate :: Name . Name", "ArgumentCoordinate :: Name . Name ( Name : )", "DirectiveCoordinate :: @ Name" and "DirectiveArgumentCoordinate :: @ Name ( Name : )". A grammar production is a requirement on what parses (Appendix A: "descriptive assertions"). A coordinate the reference accepts and the implementation rejects fails here, whatever it resolves to.
checks.note: 17 vectors whose resolution the spec leaves undefined are graded on their syntax only

checks.title: Only Names and the punctuators ( ) . : @ are tokens
checks.basis: "SchemaCoordinateToken :: SchemaCoordinatePunctuator | Name", "SchemaCoordinatePunctuator :: one of ( ) . : @", and "A {SchemaCoordinate} is a self-contained grammar with its own set of lexical tokens, it is not contained within a {Document}. The source text of a SchemaCoordinate must be a sequence of {SourceCharacter}." So `$`, `!`, a string, a number and `...` as one token are not schema coordinate tokens.

checks.title: No whitespace, line terminator, comma, comment or byte order mark anywhere
checks.basis: "Unlike other GraphQL documents, {SchemaCoordinate} must not contain {Whitespace} or other {Ignored} grammars within the character sequence. This ensures that every schema coordinates has a single unambiguous and unique lexical form." Ignored is UnicodeBOM, Whitespace, LineTerminator, Comment and Comma (§2.1.7), at the start and the end as well as between tokens.

checks.title: A type coordinate resolves to the named type, built-in scalars included, or to nothing
checks.basis: TypeCoordinate: "Return the type in {schema} named {typeName} if it exists." "A schema coordinate may refer to either a defined or built-in schema element. For example, `String` ..."; "If the schema element cannot be found, the resolve function will not yield a value (without raising an error)." Algorithm steps have the level of their algorithm (Appendix A). A built-in scalar no field, argument or input field refers to is unspecified (docs/kit/coordinate.md).

checks.title: A member coordinate resolves to the field, input field or enum value, or to nothing
checks.basis: MemberCoordinate: "If {type} is an Enum type: ... Return the enum value of {type} named {enumValueName} if it exists. Otherwise, if {type} is an Input Object type: ... Return the input field of {type} named {inputFieldName} if it exists. Otherwise: ... Return the field of {type} named {fieldName} if it exists."

checks.title: An argument coordinate resolves to the field's argument, or to nothing
checks.basis: ArgumentCoordinate: "Return the argument of {field} named {fieldArgumentName} if it exists."

checks.title: A directive coordinate resolves to the directive, @deprecated included, or to nothing
checks.basis: DirectiveCoordinate: "Return the directive in {schema} named {directiveName} if it exists." The schema applies @deprecated, and "GraphQL implementations that support the type system definition language must provide the `@deprecated` directive if representing deprecated portions of the schema" (§3.13).

checks.title: A directive argument coordinate resolves to the directive's argument, or to nothing
checks.basis: DirectiveArgumentCoordinate: "Return the argument of {directive} named {directiveArgumentName} if it exists." §2.14's own example of a built-in element is `@deprecated(reason:)`.

checks.title: A coordinate whose type, field or directive isn't in the schema raises an error
checks.basis: "However, an error will be raised if any non-leaf nodes within a schema coordinate cannot be found in the schema." The algorithms: "Assert: {type} must exist", "Assert: {field} must exist.", "Assert: {directive} must exist."

checks.title: A member or argument coordinate on a type of the wrong kind raises an error, as the Asserts say
checks.basis: MemberCoordinate: "Assert: {type} must exist, and must be an Enum, Input Object, Object or Interface type." ArgumentCoordinate: "Assert: {type} must exist, and be an Object or Interface type." The prose names only one error, "if any non-leaf nodes within a schema coordinate cannot be found", and says that if the element "cannot be found, the resolve function will not yield a value (without raising an error)". For `Date.x` on a scalar, or `SearchCriteria.filter(x:)` on an input field, every non-leaf node is found, so the prose gives no element and no error, where the Asserts give an error. Both pass; the report records which one the implementation gives. An element, or a rejected coordinate, fails.

checks.title: @skip, @include, @specifiedBy and @oneOf resolve, with their arguments, though the schema doesn't define them
checks.basis: "A schema element can be ... a directive, or a directive argument defined within a schema (including built-in types and directives)." Whether a schema has them is §3.13's: "GraphQL implementations should provide the `@skip` and `@include` directives", and "should provide the `@specifiedBy` directive if representing custom scalar definitions" and "the `@oneOf` directive if representing OneOf Input Objects", which the schema does.
